lines.japanese: うん、せっかくだから山科さんの感触を楽し──
lines.english: Yes. Since I had the chance, I might as well savor the feel of Yamashina—

lines.japanese: ──違うよ、そういうことじゃない。彼女が僕のために、一生懸命いい音楽を勧めてくれてるんだ。その心遣いに感謝しなきゃっていうことなんだ。そう、それだ。
lines.english: —No. That was not it. She was doing her utmost to introduce me to good music, all for my sake. I ought to appreciate her thoughtfulness. Yes. That was it.

lines.japanese: 「いい曲だね。じゃあ、ちょっと集中しようかな」
lines.english: “It’s a good song. All right, I think I’ll concentrate for a while.”

lines.japanese: ヘッドホンに手を添えて、それっぽいポーズをとった。意識を耳……と背中に……。
lines.english: I put a hand to the headphones and struck a suitably absorbed pose. I focused my attention on my ears... and my back...

lines.japanese: あたっ！？
lines.english: Ow?!

lines.japanese: 「でしょ！　いま流れてる曲いいよね。これってヴォーカルの人が作詞したんだけど、自分の経験に基づいて書いたんだって。共感するよね一体化するよねアインフュールングを覚えるよね」
lines.english: “Right? The song playing now is wonderful! The vocalist wrote the lyrics from personal experience. You feel what they feel, become one with them—you experience aesthetic empathy!”

lines.japanese: 山科さんはこぶしを振りまわして昂ぶっていた。
lines.english: Yamashina was waving her fists in her excitement.

lines.japanese: びしっ！　びしっ！
lines.english: Whack! Whack!

lines.japanese: びしびしばかりで、もうもにゅもにゅはないみたいだ。
lines.english: Nothing but whacks. Apparently the squooshing was over.

lines.japanese: 「うん。いい曲だね。でも、もういいかな」
lines.english: “Yeah. It’s a good song. But I think I’ve heard enough.”

lines.japanese: 「ええっ、勿体無いよちゃんと聞いてよリリックがいいんだよ、もう泣くよ号泣だよ漫画化するとぶわって音がするよ、詞の最後で主人公死ぬからもらい死にたくなるよ」
lines.english: “What? What a waste! Listen properly, the lyrics are the best part! You’ll cry, you’ll sob—if this were a manga, the tears would go fwoosh! The protagonist dies at the end and you’ll want to drop dead in sympathy!”

lines.japanese: 正直、死とか破滅とかの出てくる世界観は苦手なんだけど、彼女をここまで熱狂させるんだからひとの心に訴えるなにかはあるんだろう。
lines.english: Truthfully, I did not care for fictional worlds full of death and ruin. Still, anything that inspired this much fervor in her must have some power to move the human heart.

lines.japanese: 何度か聴いてるうちに慣れてくるものかもしれない。大切なのは自ら興味の扉を閉ざさないことだ。もしかしたら僕にも、これを機に新しい感性が生まれるかもしれない。
lines.english: Perhaps I would grow accustomed to it after a few listens. The important thing was to stay open to new interests. This might even awaken some new sensibility in me.

lines.japanese: 「これね、私の周りには良さを分かってくれるひとが少なくて、もしかして私の感性ってずれてるのかなって心配になったりもしたんだけど、羽田君がいてくれたから自信を取りもどすことができたよ、えへへ」
lines.english: “Hardly anybody around me understands what’s so good about this, and sometimes I worried that maybe my taste was all wrong. But having you here has given me my confidence back. Hehe.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、おれにもなんとなく良さが分かってきた気がするよ」
lines.english: “Yeah. I think I’m beginning to understand what’s good about it.”

lines.japanese: 「やだ嬉しい！　羽田君と私って感性がすごく近いのかもしれない、こんなひとが同じクラスにいるなんてすごいシンクロニシティだよね、どうして今まで気づかなかったんだろう」
lines.english: “Oh, I’m so happy! Maybe you and I have incredibly similar sensibilities. Finding somebody like that in my own class is amazing synchronicity. How did I never notice before?”

lines.japanese: 「ああもうっ、二年前の私に教えてあげたい、羽田君みたいな共通の楽しみを覚えられるひとが近くにいるってこと。ありがとー、ほんとありがとー、こんなに感謝したのは生まれて初めてかもしれないよ」
lines.english: “Ohhh, I wish I could tell the me of two years ago that somebody who could learn to share the things she loved was right there beside her—somebody like Haneda. Thank you! Seriously, thank you! I might never have been this grateful in my life!”

lines.japanese: 「そんな、大げさだよ。でもそこまで言ってもらえるのは嬉しいな」
lines.english: “That’s an exaggeration. But I’m happy to hear you say it.”

lines.japanese: 「私も嬉しいよ羽田君！　ねえねえ、それでね、この曲のいい所をもっと解説すると――」
lines.english: “I’m happy too, Haneda! Now, listen—if I explain some more of what makes this song so wonderful—”

lines.japanese: びしびしびしびし……！
lines.english: Whack-whack-whack-whack...!

lines.japanese: その後山科さんの解説をしばらく聞いていたけど、びしびしがもにゅもにゅに変わることはなかった。
lines.english: I listened to Yamashina’s commentary for some time after that, but the whacking never turned back into squooshing.
